title: Carbon and its Compounds - Kid-friendly science workshop with tiny lessons and quick quizzes

questions.question: What does tetravalency of carbon mean?
questions.explanation: Tetravalency means carbon has combining capacity of four.

questions.question: What does catenation mean?
options: Carbon atoms link to each other
questions.explanation: Catenation is the ability to form chains with itself.

questions.question: Why can carbon form so many compounds?
options: Because it has only one valency
questions.explanation: Those two features together create huge variety.

questions.question: A covalent bond is formed by
questions.explanation: Covalent bonding involves sharing electrons.

questions.question: Many carbon compounds are poor conductors because they are mainly
questions.explanation: Covalent compounds generally conduct poorly.

questions.question: Which element is central in food, fuels, and many living structures?
questions.explanation: Carbon chemistry is everywhere in daily life.

questions.question: What kind of shapes can carbon skeletons form?
questions.explanation: Carbon can build many structural patterns.

questions.question: Which type of compounds often has lower melting points than ionic compounds?
questions.explanation: Covalent compounds often melt more easily than ionic ones.

questions.question: A hydrocarbon contains only
questions.explanation: Hydrocarbons are made only of carbon and hydrogen.

questions.question: A saturated hydrocarbon has
options: only single bonds between carbon atoms
questions.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single carbon-carbon bonds.

questions.question: An unsaturated hydrocarbon may contain
options: only single bonds and no carbon
questions.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons include multiple bonds.

questions.question: Which type of hydrocarbon usually undergoes addition reactions more easily?
questions.explanation: Multiple bonds make addition easier.

questions.question: What is a homologous series?
options: A family of compounds with similar structures and patterns
questions.explanation: Homologous series organise compounds into related families.

questions.question: Why are homologous series useful?
options: They help you see patterns instead of memorising each compound separately
questions.explanation: Pattern recognition is the key benefit.

questions.question: Which statement fits saturated compounds best?
options: They are full of single carbon-carbon bonds
questions.explanation: Single bonds define saturation.

questions.question: Which statement fits unsaturated compounds best?
options: They contain at least one multiple bond
questions.explanation: Multiple bonds define unsaturation.

modules.name: M2: Useful Reactions of Carbon Compounds

questions.question: What is combustion?
options: Burning of a substance in oxygen
questions.explanation: Combustion means burning.

questions.question: A clean blue flame usually suggests
questions.explanation: Blue flames usually indicate better combustion.

questions.question: A smoky yellow flame suggests
questions.explanation: Soot and smoke indicate incomplete combustion.

questions.question: What does oxidation often involve?
options: Gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen
questions.explanation: Oxidation changes substances through oxygen or hydrogen changes.

questions.question: Which type of compound often undergoes addition reactions?
questions.explanation: Multiple bonds support addition reactions.

questions.question: What happens in a substitution reaction?
options: One atom or group is replaced by another
questions.explanation: Substitution means replacement.

questions.question: Why does bond type matter in carbon chemistry?
questions.explanation: Structure controls reactivity.

questions.question: Which reaction type best matches “new atoms join across a multiple bond”?
questions.explanation: That is the idea of an addition reaction.

modules.name: M3: Ethanol, Ethanoic Acid and Soap

questions.question: Which carbon compound is related to vinegar in dilute form?
questions.explanation: Vinegar contains dilute ethanoic acid.

questions.question: Which statement about ethanol is correct?
questions.explanation: Ethanol is flammable and must be handled carefully.

questions.question: Why is safe handling important even for useful chemicals?
options: Because usefulness does not remove risk
Because useful chemicals can never react
Because risk only exists in space
questions.explanation: Safety remains important for all chemicals.

questions.question: Why can soap remove oily dirt better than plain water?
options: Soap interacts with both water and oil
questions.explanation: Soap molecules have two different helpful ends.

questions.question: What is a micelle?
options: A tiny droplet structure that traps oily dirt
questions.explanation: Soap forms micelles around oily dirt.

questions.question: Which part of soap helps connect to oil?
options: The oil-loving end of the soap molecule
questions.explanation: Soap has one end that is attracted to oil.

questions.question: What makes soap a great example in science?
options: Its cleaning action is explained by molecular structure
It behaves like a noble gas
questions.explanation: Soap links molecular design with visible effects.

questions.question: Ethanoic acid belongs to which broad class of substances in this workshop?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic acid is an important carbon compound.
